m01: Golden of hue, like a doe, wearing garlands of gold and silver, shining like the moon, made of gold: bring Lakṣmī to me, O Jātavedas, Agni. ॥1॥
m02: O Jātavedas, bring to me that Lakṣmī who never goes away, with whom I may gain gold, cows, horses and men (attendants and kin). ॥2॥
m03: Her who has horses before her and chariots around her, who wakes all with the trumpeting of elephants, the goddess Śrī, I invoke; may the goddess Śrī take me lovingly as her own. ॥3॥
m04: Her who is bliss, who smiles, who is girt by walls of gold, moist with tenderness, radiant, content herself and contenting all, seated on the lotus, lotus-hued: that Śrī I invoke here. ॥4॥
m05: Shining like the moon, radiant, blazing with glory in the world, Śrī, cherished by the gods, the noble one: in her, Padminī, the lotus one, I take refuge. May Alakṣmī, my misfortune, perish; I choose you. ॥5॥
m06: O you whose hue is the sun's, the lord of the forest born of tapas, ardent heat, the bilva, is your tree. May its fruits, by tapas, drive away the illusions within and the misfortunes without. ॥6॥
m07: May the friend of the gods and fame come to me, together with the jewel. I am born in this realm; may he grant me fame and prosperity. ॥7॥
The friend of the gods is held in tradition to be Kubera.
m08: Jyeṣṭhā, Alakṣmī, foul with hunger and thirst, I destroy. Want and lack of prosperity, all of it, drive out of my house. ॥8॥
Jyeṣṭhā, 'the elder', is a name of Alakṣmī; tradition calls her Lakṣmī's elder sister.
m09: Her who is known by her fragrance, whom none can overcome, ever thriving, rich in the dung of herds, the sovereign of all beings: that Śrī I invoke here. ॥9॥
m10: May we win the desire of the mind and its intent, and the truth of speech. May the beauty of cattle and of food, may Śrī and fame, abide in me. ॥10॥
m11: Through Kardama Śrī has come to have offspring; O Kardama, come to be in me. Make Śrī, the mother garlanded with lotuses, dwell in my family. ॥11॥
Kardama ('mud, moist earth') and Ciklīta ('moisture') are held in tradition to be sons of Śrī.
m12: May the waters bring forth things smooth and rich; O Ciklīta, dwell in my house, and make the goddess, mother Śrī, dwell in my family. ॥12॥
m13: Moist with tenderness, like a lotus pool, nourishment itself, golden-tawny, garlanded with lotuses, shining like the moon, made of gold: bring Lakṣmī to me, O Jātavedas. ॥13॥
m14: Moist with tenderness, like a she-elephant, a staff to lean on, fair of hue, garlanded with gold, shining like the sun, made of gold: bring Lakṣmī to me, O Jātavedas. ॥14॥
m15: O Jātavedas, bring to me that Lakṣmī who never goes away, with whom I may gain gold in plenty, cows, maidservants, horses and men. ॥15॥
m16: Let one who is pure and self-restrained offer ghee into the fire every day and also recite the fifteen-verse hymn constantly, desiring Śrī. ॥16॥
m17: O lotus-faced one, O lotus-thighed, O lotus-eyed, O lotus-born, take me as your own, O lotus-eyed one, so that I may gain happiness. ॥17॥
m18: O giver of horses, giver of cows, giver of wealth, O you of great wealth, O Devī, may wealth favour me, and grant me all that I desire. ॥18॥
m19: Give me sons and grandsons, wealth, grain, elephants, horses and the like, cows and a chariot. You are the mother of creatures; may she make me long-lived. ॥19॥
m20: Agni is wealth, Vāyu is wealth, Sūrya is wealth, the Vasu is wealth. Indra and Bṛhaspati are wealth; wealth reaches Varuṇa. ॥20॥
m21: O Vainateya, son of Vinatā, drink the Soma; may Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, drink the Soma. May he give me the Soma of the Soma-offerer's wealth. ॥21॥
m22: Neither anger nor envy, neither greed nor an evil mind arise in devotees who have done good deeds; one should recite the Śrī Sūkta. ॥22॥
m23: O radiant one, may your lightnings from the cloud of the sky pour down rain. May every seed sprout; protect the Veda, strike down those who hate. ॥23॥
m24: O lover of the lotus, O Padminī, O you with a lotus in hand, O dweller in the lotus, O you with eyes long as lotus petals, O beloved of the world, O you in accord with Viṣṇu's mind, set your lotus feet within me. ॥24॥
m25: She who sits on a lotus seat, with broad hips and with eyes long as lotus leaves, whose navel is a deep whirlpool, who is bowed by the weight of her breasts, whose garment and upper cloth are white, ॥25॥
m26: Lakṣmī, bathed by heavenly lordly elephants from golden pots studded with clusters of gems: may she, with a lotus in her hand, ever dwell in my house, endowed with every auspiciousness. ॥26॥
m27: Lakṣmī, daughter of the king of the ocean of milk, queen of the abode of Śrīraṅga, whose handmaids are all the wives of the gods, the one flame of the lamp for the worlds, ॥27॥
m28: by whose graceful, gentle glance Brahmā, Indra and Śiva who bears the Gaṅgā won their glory: you, mistress of the household of the three worlds, born of the lake, beloved of Mukunda, I bow to. ॥28॥
m29: Siddhalakṣmī, Mokṣalakṣmī, Jayalakṣmī, Sarasvatī, Śrīlakṣmī and Varalakṣmī: may she be gracious to me always. ॥29॥
m30: Bearing in her hands the gesture of boon and the goad, the noose and the gesture of fearlessness, who sits on a lotus seat, who has the splendour of ten million rising suns and three eyes: you, the first one, sovereign of the world, I worship. ॥30॥
m31: O auspiciousness of all that is auspicious, O Śivā, the auspicious one, accomplisher of every aim, O giver of refuge, O three-eyed one, O Devī, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥31॥
m32: O dweller in the lotus, O you with a lotus in hand, O you made beautiful by the whitest garment, fragrance and garland, O Bhagavatī, beloved of Hari, lovely one, bringer of prosperity to the three worlds, be gracious to me. ॥32॥
m33: Viṣṇu's consort, forbearance itself, the goddess, Mādhavī, beloved of Mādhava, the dear companion of Viṣṇu, the goddess beloved of Acyuta, I bow to. ॥33॥
m34: May we know Mahālakṣmī and meditate on Viṣṇu's consort; may that Lakṣmī impel us. ॥34॥
m35: The purifying Pavamāna is glorified; may it bestow the radiance of Śrī, long life and health, and wealth, grain, cattle, the gain of many sons, and a long life of a hundred years. ॥35॥
m36: Debt, disease and the like, poverty, sin, hunger and untimely death, fear, grief and anguish of mind: may all these of mine perish for ever. ॥36॥
m37: He who knows thus. Om. May we know Mahādevī and meditate on Viṣṇu's consort; may that Lakṣmī impel us. Om, peace, peace, peace. ॥37॥
